O.statement: At the measured revision tools/reopen-row.py answers the round-62 closure's routed defects: (1) every redirect target of a fetched URL is re-validated against the private-host refusal before it is requested, and a redirect hop to an authority (host, port) different from the fetching URL's is refused even under --allow-private, so a public URL 302-ing to loopback/RFC1918 is never fetched; (2) a registry row whose URL is malformed (unparseable port, unbalanced bracketed IPv6, empty host) prints `ROW <ID> MALFORMED attempts=0 url=-`, attempts no request, shows no traceback, and the run's exit is 1, not 2; (3) a response with Content-Encoding: gzip is decompressed before matching; (4) a body read that reaches the 4 MiB cap without EOF is not matched silently: when the quote is absent from the read bytes the verdict is TRUNCATED (ranked with ABSENT) and when the quote is inside the read bytes the verdict is still LOCATED; (5) --timeout SECONDS (default 30) is a per-request wall budget covering connect, headers and body, so a stalling body cannot outlive it; (6) each request in a redirect chain counts as an attempt and at most 5 hops are followed. The capability's safety hold lifts only when the counter passes AND the three named independent review reports (RevToolA/RevToolB/RevToolC wave seats, re-run by RevHoldLift on the landed bytes) record no open HIGH or MEDIUM finding against the landed source.
